title: Forms II, III, and IV
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 20; Ryding Ch. 23–25)
objectives: Conjugate Forms II (فَعَّلَ), III (فَاعَلَ), and IV (أَفْعَلَ) in past and imperfect.
Identify the characteristic ḍammah on imperfect prefixes (يُـ) in Forms II–IV.
Recognize the standard maṣdar patterns: تَفْعِيلٌ, مُفَاعَلَةٌ / فِعَالٌ, and إِفْعَالٌ.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 19: What prefix do ALL derived participles (Forms II–X) share?

sections.heading: The Causative & Associative Stems
sections.body: Forms II, III, and IV are the only derived forms whose imperfect prefix takes ḍammah (يُفَعِّلُ, يُفَاعِلُ, يُفْعِلُ). Form II (doubled C2) expresses causativity or intensity; Form III (long ā after C1) expresses directed or associative effort; Form IV (prefixed أَـ) expresses causativity or entering a state/time.

sections.label: Hamzat al-Qaṭʿ in Form IV
sections.summary: Unlike Forms VII–X (which begin with elidable hamzat al-waṣl), Form IV past, imperative, and maṣdar (أَفْعَلَ, أَفْعِلْ, إِفْعَالٌ) ALWAYS begin with disjunctive hamzat al-qaṭʿ.

sections.translation: The teacher taught the pupils Arabic.
sections.irab: عَلَّمَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ (وَزْنُ فَعَّلَ) | المُعَلِّمُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ | التَّلَامِيذَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ أَوَّلُ | العَرَبِيَّةَ: مَفْعُولٌ بِهِ ثَانٍ
sections.notes: Because Form II (عَلَّمَ) is causative of Form I (عَلِمَ 'knew'), it takes two direct objects ('taught [someone] [something]').

sections.heading: Spotting Form IV in Imperfect
sections.body: In the imperfect of Form IV (يُنْزِلُ), the initial أَ disappears, leaving only the ḍammah on the prefix (يُـ) and sukūn on the first radical.
